---
title: "How do I estimate the probability of an event from observed trials?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I estimate the probability of an event from observed trials?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Count qualifying events and total trials.

2. Divide successes by total when the denominator is positive.

3. State the sample size and what counts as an event.

## Runnable example

```{r}
events <- c(TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE)
successes <- sum(events)
trials <- length(events)
p <- successes/trials
print(c(successes=successes,trials=trials,rate=p))
```

## Interpret the result

Five successes among eight recorded trials give an observed event proportion of 0.625, or 62.5%. This is an estimate for a broader chance only under suitable sampling conditions.

## Check before using your own data

An observed proportion is not necessarily the true probability for the wider population, especially with a small or biased sample.
